newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen testing resistance.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen testing resistance.

text.p: Polish shares on Monday fell after a three-session rise and analysts said investors would be watching whether the main market, currently at 14,421.6 points, would prove strong enough to pierce resistance at 14,500.

"If 14,500 is pierced we can keep going up but if there's already stronger selling after price-fixing on Tuesday then we might have to wait for the rises after some falls," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
But analysts said the central bank's comments it might raise interest rates as soon as mid-January to curb fast credit growth was cooling some players' enthusiasm.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.4 percent to 14,421.6 and turnover rose 15.7 percent to 98.2 million zlotys ($34.1 million) on both markets.
Losers led gainers by 58 to 15 with 10 stocks flat.
Analysts said 14,000 might provide support should there be falls.
They said investors would be watching the food price figures for the last 10 days in December due on Wednesday to help determine if interest rates would need raising.
Analysts said some large orders at order balancing suggested institutional investors were active.
They said biggest loser construction firm Espebepe, down 6.7 percent, fell in profit-taking after a 45.2-percent speculative surge. The stock had previously plunged on a bankruptcy threat.
Analysts also said software firm ComputerLand, down 3.4 percent in active trade, fell in profit-taking after having reached a 52-week high on Friday.
Mass privatisation NFI units fell 0.7 percent to 142 zlotys in a turnover of 16.1 million zlotys.
